newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev firms on c-bank support.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev firms on c-bank support.

text.p: Dollar sales by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) supported the lev to 222-223 per dollar at the close of the interbank market from 225-227 at noon but still down from 216-219 at the opening, dealers said.
"The lev regained some ground on central bank support to close at 222-223 to the dollar," a commercial bank dealer said.
The lev eased to 229 in some deals in the early afternoon pressured by high foreign currency demand and excessively low supply, traders said. @
At that moment the dollar was bid at 230-232 levs, but some dealers said they doubted whether there were any deals at those levels.
Then the BNB started offering dollars between 222 and 225 levs, which calmed the market down and boosted the lev, dealers said.
Central bank officials declined comment on the amounts of foreign currency involved in the sales by the BNB or whether they were offered directly to end clients. @

In a bid to relieve pressure on the lev the BNB today decided to cut to 10 percent from 20 percent the share of minimum required reserves that commercial banks are allowed to use daily as an overdraft on their settlement accounts at the BNB.
According to dealers the decision, to go in force on Wednesday, will slow down the lev's decline.
"Some banks with long dollar positions will probably sell small dollar volumes in a bid to improve their lev liquidity while others will lack levs to buy foreign currency," a trader said. @

The previous cut of minimum reserves from 50 percent to 20 percent two weeks ago contained the lev's fall from 219 per dollar at the close on August 20 to around 202 per dollar a week later. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
